Interface StaticResources

All Superinterfaces:
RequestHandler, ResourceHandler
public sealed interface StaticResources extends ResourceHandler
Static resources served by a handler route: the files under a directory, or the resources under a package of the classpath, including those inside jars. 
routes.GET("/assets").resources(StaticResources.classpath("public").cacheControl("public, max-age=31536000, immutable"));
routes.path("/docs", docs -> docs.GET("").resources(StaticResources.fileSystem("/var/www/docs")));
routes.GET("/files/{+path}", StaticResources.of("file:/srv/files", "classpath:files").indexFile(null));

The handler reads the path of the resource, relative to the base, from the path variable ResourceHandler.pathVariable(), path by default, see HttpRouteSpec.resources(ResourceHandler). It answers 404 when no location has the resource, when the path is a directory without an index file, when the path tries to leave the base: a . or .. segment, a backslash, a colon, a NUL character, an absolute path or a dot, slash or backslash encoded twice, when the path is another spelling of a path the router may route elsewhere: an empty segment or an encoded slash or backslash, and when a segment of the path is hidden, i.e. starts with a dot, e.g. .env, unless hiddenFiles(boolean) serves them.

A file of the file system is a SystemFile, and any other resource, e.g. in a jar, a StreamedFile. The file body writers of the server answer them like the files of the static resources of micronaut.router.static-resources, to GET and HEAD alike: the content type from the file name, the Last-Modified and cache headers, 304 to a matching If-Modified-Since, and, for the files of the file system, 206 to a Range.

Reading the resources blocks, so the routes of resources run on the blocking executor, unless the route or its group declares an executor, see ResourceHandler.blocking().

The instances are immutable: each option returns a copy with the option set.

5.3.0

    • indexFile

      StaticResources indexFile(@Nullable String name)
      The index file of a directory: the resource of an empty path, e.g. the URI prefix of HttpRouteSpec.resources(ResourceHandler), and of a path without an extension that is not a resource, e.g. docs for docs/index.html.
      Parameters:
      name - The name of the index file, "index.html" by default, or null for none
      Returns:
      A copy with the index file
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the name is empty, . or .., or has a slash, a backslash or a colon
